title: Microsoft and Chevron Sign 20-Year Power Deal For Texas Data Center
source_used: Data Center Knowledge (23 Jun 2026) for the deal; The Next Web (1 Oct 2026, relaying Semafor) for the delay; EnergyNow page returned 403
key_facts: Chevron and Microsoft signed a 20-year agreement, announced on Monday 22 Jun 2026, to supply dedicated power to a planned Microsoft data centre campus near Pecos, Texas (Project Kilby).
A co-located natural gas plant will supply it, developed by Chevron subsidiary Energy Forge One and investment firm Engine No. 1; about 2.67 GW built in phases, first power planned for 2028.
Chevron said it expects a final investment decision by the end of 2026.
Microsoft said the campus will add roughly 2 GW of data centre capacity over five to seven years and create more than 6,000 construction jobs and hundreds of permanent jobs.
Most turbines come from GE Vernova, with more from Solar Turbines, a Caterpillar subsidiary.
ERCOT, the Texas grid operator, has questioned in planning documents how much announced AI demand will materialise (Data Center Knowledge).

The Next Web, relaying Semafor on 1 Oct 2026: the final investment decision could slip from the end of 2026 to 2027 because of state politics, after Governor Greg Abbott ordered a stop to all new environmental permits for data centres until state grid and water agencies finish audits; Chevron says power is still on track for 2028.
quote_evidence: Chevron said it expects to reach a final investment decision by the end of 2026.
The deal formalizes discussions disclosed in April.
A final investment decision on Project Kilby, a huge gas-powered data centre in West Texas, could slip from the end of this year to 2027 because of state politics.
why_it_matters_hint: A dedicated gas plant beside a Microsoft campus shows how AI data centres secure their own power, but the project still needs its final investment decision and Texas permits.
notes: OLD NEWS RE-DATED: EnergyNow URL carries /2026/06/ and Google News lists the same deal on 22 Jun 2026 from Business Wire (Chevron release), CNBC, Bloomberg, WSJ, Yahoo Finance; EnergyNow re-published it on 11 Oct 2026. Sources differ on the joint-venture partner (Data Center Knowledge: Engine No. 1; The Next Web: Joulent, which grew out of Engine No. 1), so the summary leaves it out. Business Wire, CNBC and EnergyNow pages were blocked here.
